title: רב פפא סתם
author: Heilprin source tradition; Warsaw digital witness

paragraphs: (1) A pupil of Rava: Tosafot, Shabbat 93a; Rashi, Eruvin 26a. In Rava's name: there; Pesahim 7, end of a; Megillah 26b; Avodah Zarah 8b—‘in Rav's name’ should read ‘Rava,’ as it does in the Amsterdam printing; Bava Batra 126a. Rav Pappa said, ‘Rava tested us’: Eruvin 51a; Mo'ed Katan 13, end of a; Nedarim 90b; Menahot 91b; Bekhorot 47a—‘Rabbah tested us’ is a scribal error and should read ‘Rava’; in the new Shas [שס״ח; source-edition abbreviation, uncollated] it was not corrected [ל״ת, provisional reading]. It should likewise read this way in Ketubbot 61a. See above, Rav Huna bar Hinena.

(2) He married a priest's daughter and ate on account of his wife: Hullin 132a. He was wealthy: Arvei Pesahim 111b, ‘his hour was favorable’ (see above, Abaye). So it also appears at the end of Horayot (see above, Rav Huna bar Rav Yehoshua; he ate much—see there). He married Abba of Sura's daughter, and his son, Abba Mar, likewise married Abba of Sura's daughter: Rashi, Ketubbot 52b. Rava called him ‘sudani,’ Berakhot 44b. Rashi explains that he brewed beer, in keeping with the saying, ‘With dates in your basket, run to the brewer's house’; as it says in Arvei Pesahim 113a, ‘Had I not brewed beer, I would not have become rich.’ In Shabbat 140b, Rav Pappa said: ‘One who can drink beer but drinks wine violates “Do not destroy.”’ Hiddushei Aggadot writes that this was because he brewed beer for sale. In Niddah 12, beginning of b, Rashi explains sudani: another explanation is ‘Torah scholar,’ after ‘The Lord's secret is for those who fear Him.’ The Arukh writes ‘one who fears Heaven,’ as it is written, ‘The Lord's secret is for those who fear Him.’ In Menahot 71a, Rashi gives two explanations. Were I not afraid, I would explain that he called him this after his father-in-law, Abba Surani. He fasted for saying ‘these rabbis’: Helek, 100, beginning of a.

(3) Rav Nahman called him ‘bar ushpizta,’ Ta'anit 24b. Rashi explains (it is not in Rashi, but in the Arukh, entry בר) that this was his mother's name (see above, Rav Nahman bar Ushpizta). Perhaps this is the origin of the pious man's received tradition that Rav Pappa had no known father (see above, R' Zeira), since Rav Nahman called him by his mother's name. Yuhasin writes [under aleph, at ‘Rav Pappa's father’]: ‘But in Bava Metzia 28b, Rav Pappa's father came before Rabbah bar Rav Huna. In Sotah’ (a scribal error; it should read Yevamot 106a), ‘a daughter of Rav Pappa's father-in-law fell before an unsuitable levir. He came before Abaye,’ etc. ‘Abaye asked Rav Pappa, “Where is your father?” He answered, “In town.” “Where is your mother?” He answered, “In town.” He set his eyes upon him, and he died’ (see there). Thus he did have a known father. End quotation. He walked on Abaye's right (see there). Tosafot, Arvei Pesahim, write that he walked somewhat to the side, for Yoma 37a says that one who walks to his teacher's right is an ignoramus. Abaye called him “orphan,” Ketubbot 17b:3 [Heilprin’s text has yatmei].

(4) In Pesahim 112b: ‘Do not sit on an Aramean woman's bed,’ because of the episode involving Rav Pappa. Rashi, Rashbam, and the Arukh, entry ארם, explain that a gentile woman owed him money, and he used to enter her house every day to collect it. One day she strangled her son and placed him in her bed. When Rav Pappa came, she told him, ‘Sit until I bring your money,’ and he did so. When she returned she said, ‘You killed my son!’ He fled from the region. End quotation. Yet in the first chapter of Berakhot, 8b: ‘Do not sit on an Aramean woman's bed,’ because of Rav Pappa's episode. He went to an Aramean woman, who spread the bed for him and said, ‘Sit.’ He told her, ‘I will not sit until you lift the bed.’ She lifted the bed, and he found a dead infant there. ‘From this they said: one may not sit on an Aramean woman's bed.’ End quotation. This is the opposite of what they wrote. Perhaps they found a different episode in some aggadah, and this happened to him twice; after the accusation against him, he was cautious. But it is difficult: how did they say in Berakhot, ‘From this they said: one may not sit,’ etc., when it was from the episode of the accusation against him that they said one may not sit on an Aramean woman's bed? This needs examination.

(5) Rav Pappa presided after Rava and Abaye, as is evident in the last chapter of Mo'ed Katan. The pupils did not know whether Rav Pappa had stated it on his own authority or in his teacher's name: Shabbat 27a; Tosafot, Shevuot 26, beginning of a. He dreamed that he entered a marsh and became head of an academy: Berakhot 57a. At Naresh, near Sura, in the year 4113, for nineteen years or thirteen years; he died in 4132, or 4132, or 4135 [the repeated 4132 is in the source]. See Part I, 4113, and see there, year 4234, what I wrote. Rav Pappa happened to come to Tavakh (a place-name), and Rav and Shmuel were there [wording as transmitted]. He went to his house and questioned him, etc. Rav Pappa left his lodging because they had embarrassed him; Rav Shimi bar Ashi came before him: Niddah 33b. He said, ‘May the Merciful One save us from the embarrassment caused by Shimi bar Ashi,’ who used to raise many objections to Rav Pappa. Rav Shimi accepted silence upon himself and no longer challenged him: Ta'anit 9, beginning of b. Rav Huna bar Manoah, Rav Shmuel bar Idi, and R' Hiyya of Vastanya used to attend Rava. When Rava died they came before Rav Pappa. When he raised a point of law, they did not reach the same understanding as they had with Rava, and they signaled to one another. He was distressed. They read to him in a dream, ‘I cut off the three shepherds’ (Heaven wished to punish them because they had embarrassed him). When they took leave of him he told them, ‘Let the rabbis go be-shalam,’ Ta'anit there. In Ein Yaakov the reading is ‘le-shalama,’ in keeping with Berakhot's saying that one taking leave of a friend should not say ‘Go be-shalom.’ Although it appeared to him in his dream that they would be punished, he would not say this, for ‘Even to punish the righteous is not good.’ In Kiddushin 32, beginning of b, Rav Pappa was serving drinks at his son Abba Mar's wedding. He lifted a cup for R' Yitzhak son of Rav Yehudah, who did not rise before him, and he took offense. He said there: although a teacher who waives his honor has waived it, he should have made a gesture of respect (moving a little as though wishing to rise before him). End quotation. Yuhasin, under yod, writes, ‘Yitzhak, Rav Pappa's pupil, at Abba Mar's wedding, first chapter of Kiddushin.’ End quotation. It appears that he did not read ‘Rav Yitzhak son of Rav Yehudah’ in the wedding episode, but ‘Yitzhak, Rav Pappa's pupil.’ Faithful evidence for this is that he necessarily gave Rav Yitzhak bar Rav Yehudah a separate entry there. This also appears reasonable because Rav Yitzhak, his son, was the father of the father of Homa, whom Abaye married after her two husbands died. Abaye died soon after their marriage; Rava presided for fourteen years after Abaye's death, and afterward Rav Pappa presided, etc. Rava was born when Rav Yehudah died. Thus Rav Yitzhak bar Rav Yehudah was presumably old at Abba Mar's marriage. Rav Yitzhak was great in Torah: he repeatedly challenged his father's statements, and the halakhah follows him (see there). In Arvei Pesahim, Rav Yehudah sent his son Rav Yitzhak to see how Ulla would recite havdalah; he in turn sent Abaye. This indicates that he was greater than Abaye. Still more: Yalta, Rav Nahman's wife, sent to Rav Yitzhak bar Rav Yehudah to inspect her blood. He thus issued a ruling in the jurisdiction of Rav Nahman, Rava's teacher. How, then, could Rav Pappa take offense at him for not rising before him, as though he were his pupil? It therefore appears that in the episode at Abba Mar's wedding it was not Rav Yitzhak bar Rav Yehudah, but another Yitzhak, Rav Pappa's pupil. Understand this. Responsa Zekan Aharon, section 25, writes that Rav Pappa was an expert physician: he saw that Rav Huna bar Rav Yehoshua was ill and said, ‘Prepare provisions for him’ (see there). In Shabbat 119a, he twisted wicks in honor of Shabbat. In Hullin 105, end of b, a demon was in his house and served him. In Pesahim 110a, Yosef the demon spoke to him. ‘Rav Pappa said, “This is what people say”’: Helek, 95a–b, 96a, 103a, 106. For his burial place, see above, Rav Yosef bar Hama.

(6) Abba Mar, his son (see above). Avital Safra in his name. Bar Abba, or Adda of Sevola, came before him. Abaye was his teacher. Rav Adda bar Ahavah expounded before him. Rav Avya the Elder spoke to him. Before Rav Aha bar Yaakov. Rav Idi bar Avin, the carpenter. Amemar in his name. He spoke to Rav Ashi. He sat behind Rav Bibi bar Avin. Guryon spoke to him. Rav Huna bar Manoah was his pupil. Rav Huna bar Ika called him ‘master’ and challenged Rav Pappa, and Rav Pappa was embarrassed. Rav Huna bar Rav Yehoshua was his colleague. Huna bar Rav Nahman, or Huna Mar, married his daughter. Before Rav Hamnuna. He raised an objection to Rav Zevid. Mar Zutra in his name. R' Hiyya of Vastini was his pupil. R' Hiyya bar Rav of Difti spoke to him. He spoke to R' Hama. He spoke to R' Hama of Nehardea. R' Hama bar Yosef was in his time. Rav Pappa said, ‘Rav Hananya taught.’ R' Hisda said: Avodah Zarah 22, beginning of b. Rav Yehudah bar Marimar before him. Rav Yosef, son of Rav Salla the pious, expounded before him. Rav Yosef son of Rava. Yosef bar Shemaya spoke to him. Rav Yosef bar Rav Shmuel spoke to him. Yosef the demon spoke to him (see above). R' Yitzhak was his pupil (see above). Rav Yeimar bar Shelemya sent to him. Rav Kahana spoke to him: Ketubbot 86a; Gittin 89b. Rav Mesharshiya was in his generation, and his son asked him. Rav Nehemya bar Yosef. Rav Nehemya bar Rav Yehoshua. Rav Nahman bar Yitzhak spoke to him. Rav Natan, Rav Huna's father, before him. Rav Sama bar Rav Yeiva spoke to him. Rav Pappa bar Abba asked him, and his sons spoke to Rav Pappa. He instructed Pappa the cattle dealer (a broker of oxen—Rashi), Gittin 19, end of a. Also Rav Pappi. Rava was his teacher (see above), and called him and Rav Huna bar Rav Yehoshua ‘white geese’ (see there). Rav Natan before him. Rav bar Sheva challenged him. Rav bar Rav Sherevya had a case before him (see Rav bar Sheva). Rabbah of Parshunya: Yuhasin writes that he was in his time; this needs examination there. Also Rava bar Shmuel. Ravin the Elder. Rami bar Abba: needs examination. Shimi bar Ashi was his pupil (see above). Shimi bar Yosef spoke to him. Shimi bar Adda spoke to him. R' Shimi bar Abba. R' Shimi bar Ze'ira, or Ziri, before him. Shimi bar Rav Idi called him ‘master.’ Rav Shmuel bar Aha before him. At Mar Shmuel's house. ר״ש bar R' Yosi [provisionally R' Shimon]. R' Shmuel bar Shimi expounded before him. R' Shmuel bar Abba. ר״ש bar Idi [provisionally Rav Shmuel] was his pupil. Rav Shemen spoke to him. Rav Sheshet bar Rav Idi spoke to him.
